subject: economics
topicDisplay: The Role Of Markets And Money
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A fall in the cost of raw materials used by a firm will:
options: Shift the demand curve to the right
Cause a contraction in supply only
Shift the supply curve to the left
Shift the supply curve to the right
questions.explain: Lower production costs increase supply at every price, shifting the supply curve right.

questions.q: The main reason people save part of their income is to:
options: Reduce the value of their money
Set money aside for future spending or emergencies
questions.explain: Saving allows people to build funds for future needs, emergencies or large purchases.

questions.q: A key feature of a monopoly compared with a competitive market is:
options: Free and easy entry for new firms
A single (or dominant) firm able to influence the price
questions.explain: A monopoly is a single dominant seller able to act as a price maker, unlike competitive price takers.

questions.q: If demand is price ELASTIC, a firm that lowers its price will see total revenue:
questions.explain: When demand is elastic, the rise in quantity outweighs the lower price, so total revenue rises.

questions.q: A fall in consumer incomes will, for a normal good, cause:
options: A movement up the demand curve
A rightward shift of the demand curve
A leftward shift of the demand curve
questions.explain: For a normal good, lower incomes reduce demand at every price, shifting the demand curve left.

questions.q: If many people lose confidence and rush to withdraw their money at once, a bank faces:
options: A bank run, risking it running out of cash
questions.explain: A loss of confidence can cause a bank run, where mass withdrawals leave the bank short of cash.

questions.q: The 'store of value' function of money means money:
options: Can be saved and used to buy goods in the future
Is accepted in exchange for goods
Can be used to compare the prices of goods
questions.explain: Money is a store of value because it holds purchasing power over time and can be saved.

questions.q: A mortgage is an example of:
options: A long-term loan used to buy property
A short-term loan to buy food
questions.explain: A mortgage is a long-term loan, usually secured against property, repaid with interest over many years.

questions.q: A good with price elasticity of demand of exactly 1 (unit elastic) means a price change leaves:
questions.explain: With unit elastic demand, the percentage change in quantity equals the percentage change in price, so revenue is unchanged.

questions.q: The 'rationing' function of the price mechanism means that when a good becomes scarce:
options: Its rising price discourages some buyers, sharing out the limited supply
questions.explain: A higher price rations scarce goods by pricing out some buyers so the limited quantity is shared.

questions.q: The 'unit of account' function of money means money:
options: Can be stored for the future
Provides a common measure to express and compare prices
questions.explain: As a unit of account, money provides a standard measure for expressing the value of goods.

questions.q: One important role of the Bank of England is to:
options: Issue banknotes and act as the country's central bank
questions.explain: The Bank of England issues currency and acts as the UK's central bank, overseeing monetary policy.

questions.q: Supply tends to be more price INELASTIC when:
options: There are many ways to switch resources
Production takes a long time and cannot be increased quickly
Firms have lots of spare capacity
questions.explain: Supply is inelastic when output cannot be increased quickly, for example crops that take a season to grow.

questions.q: A surplus in a free market is normally eliminated as:
options: Price falls until demand equals supply
questions.explain: A surplus pushes price down until quantity demanded again equals quantity supplied at equilibrium.

questions.q: Interest, from a saver's point of view, is best described as:
options: The reward for saving or lending money
A fall in the value of money
questions.explain: Interest is the reward paid to savers and lenders for providing funds.

questions.q: If the equilibrium price of a good rises after demand increases, the price has acted as a:
options: Signal and incentive for producers to supply more
questions.explain: A higher price signals to producers and gives them an incentive to expand output.

questions.q: A demerit good, such as cigarettes, is one that:
options: Has no effect on third parties
Is provided free by the government
Is over-consumed because consumers ignore its true costs
questions.explain: Demerit goods are over-consumed because people underestimate their private and external costs.

questions.q: Luxury goods tend to have demand that is price:
questions.explain: Luxuries are not essential and often have substitutes, so their demand is relatively price elastic.

questions.q: A merit good such as education is one that is:
options: Under-consumed because consumers undervalue its wider benefits
questions.explain: Merit goods are under-consumed because their full social benefits are undervalued by individuals.

questions.q: Higher interest rates are likely to slow the housing market because:
options: Mortgage repayments become more expensive, reducing demand for loans
questions.explain: Higher rates raise mortgage costs, reducing borrowing and demand for houses.

questions.q: The financial sector helps the economy by:
options: Setting the price of all goods
Channelling funds from savers to borrowers and investors
questions.explain: The financial sector links savers and borrowers, allowing investment and economic activity to take place.

questions.q: Money acts as a 'medium of exchange' because it:
options: Is widely accepted in return for goods and services
Allows value to be saved for the future
questions.explain: As a medium of exchange, money is generally accepted in payment, removing the need for barter.
